walkthroughs.body_html:
Decision Making to Improve Marketing Performance — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Decision Making to Improve Marketing Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Decision Making to Improve Marketing Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Modigliani and Miller's irrelevance theorem was published in:

options: Annual cost calculation
Cost of capital
Capital ceiling
Credit cycle

mcqs.q: What is a brand in marketing?
options: The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
A brand is just the logo on a product.
A combination of name, design, symbols and associations that distinguishes a product and creates customer perception and loyalty — more than just a logo.
A brand is the company that makes a product.

mcqs.q: What three Ps are added to make the extended marketing mix (7Ps)?
options: The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
The 7Ps are just the 4Ps repeated with different words.
A franchise is when employees buy shares in their company.
People (staff/service quality), Process (how the service is delivered), and Physical Evidence (tangible cues — uniforms, packaging, branding) — added to make the 4Ps relevant to services marketing.
An arrangement where a franchisor grants a franchisee the right to use their brand, products and systems in exchange for fees and a share of revenue.
A franchise is when employees buy shares in their company.
A franchise is when a business owns multiple branches itself.
A brand is the company that makes a product.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Gearing”?
options: Weighted average cost of debt and equity (WACC); used as discount rate for investment appraisal.
Mix of debt and equity; Modigliani-Miller (1958) showed in perfect markets capital structure is irrelevant.
Debt (loans, bonds), equity (shares), retained earnings, leasing, factoring; each has cost and risk implications.
Debt / (debt + equity); high gearing magnifies returns but raises financial risk; UK FTSE 100 average around 30%.
